target_customer: Commercial property owners and tenants in the SF Bay Area (and Nashville) needing office, lab and retail buildouts
problem: Commercial construction is slow, opaque on price and fragmented between design and building.
business_model: General contractor charging project fees, using in-house software for budgeting and delivery

founders.name: Anthony Cirinelli
previous_startups: Buildzen (co-founder, per YC page; outcome not found)

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly construction services with internal software for budgeting and tracking; no hard technical breakthrough required.

defensibility.rationale: General contracting is a relationship business with many established firms; software helps efficiency but is copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No evidence found of incumbents acting against it; it keeps operating.

market_need_then: Commercial construction was widely seen as low in productivity and slow to adopt software; strong Bay Area tenant improvement demand. No specific citation found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Tagline Built Different on the company site; emphasizes teamwork, transparency, quality, innovation

branding.brand_signature: Built Different tagline on its own site

brand_strength.rationale: Little press on the brand itself; a rebrand from X3 Builders is noted by a profile site only.

outcome_analysis: Aecore, previously X3 Builders, remains a small active commercial contractor with offices in San Jose and Nashville and recognizable corporate clients on its site. No acquisition, shutdown or large funding was found, so it looks like a steady services business rather than a venture scale outcome. Little public information limits any stronger conclusion.
notes: A profile site (yespress.io) says seed funding came from YC and CEMEX Ventures in 2019; this was not confirmed by an opened primary source (the CEMEX article fetch returned empty), so no round is recorded. Founding year conflicts: YC says 2018, a profile says 2016. Competitor list empty: no source dated near 2017 found. Founders list from YC page only; Bell prior startup Net30 appears only on a profile site.
